absent: Conditions deciding when idmapped vectors are required and physical layout of hardened vector blobs.
Numeric values for handle offset, maximum VM count, stack size, page protections, HCR and VTCR fields, and order limits.
Implementation and failure modes of table creation, host share plus unshare plus donate, pin plus unpin, donated map plus unmap, and SVE size helpers.
Full struct layouts for pools, pages, pagetables, MMUs, VM descriptors, init parameters, host data, and sysreg descriptors.
Hypercall number binding, vector slot addressing details, and per-CPU vector consumption.
Stage-two walker callbacks, cache and TLB maintenance semantics, and ordering beyond the shown barriers.
Allocation and lifetime of the VM table itself and of the I/O base plus vmemmap globals outside the shown setup.

findings.text: Hypervisor private address services reserve a forward-only carve-out and install table entries for vectors, identity code and stacks. One helper reserves a sized range under a global guard, another combines reservation with mapping while preserving sub-page offset, and setup helpers establish an executable identity window plus a hardened vector area plus aligned stacks with a guard page.

Protected virtual machine management provides reservation plus release plus initialization plus stage-two preparation plus teardown plus one-shot host protection. Reservation returns an opaque handle for a reserved slot, release clears only reserved slots, initialization pins host state and installs donated regions before publishing, and finalization arms host translation.

Stage-two table lifecycle allocates an exactly sized root from caller-supplied memory operations, records address width plus start level plus callbacks plus owning MMU, orders the allocation for hardware walkers, and later tears down the covered range before freeing the root extent and clearing references.

Host support helpers map per-CPU save areas when the feature exists, refresh per-CPU boot records with the live root address plus cache maintenance, validate strict ordering of the protected register descriptor array, and initialize a bounded buddy pool with per-order free lists.

Hypercall entry points unpack integer or address arguments from numbered host registers, translate host addresses where required, invoke the corresponding privileged helper, and return status or an allocated address through a result register. Private mapping failures crossing the exception boundary are encoded as pointer errors rather than writing through a caller pointer, and release without a result performs no return update.

Private allocation only advances a recorded cursor, rejects empty or backwards starts, rounds length to page granularity, and refuses to cross an upper vmemmap limit. Identity setup derives I/O base plus cursor plus vmemmap split from the identity range and configured address width so that I/O and vmemmap occupy a quarter that avoids the identity window, with I/O in the lower half and vmemmap in the upper half.

Private mapping expands the requested length to cover the offset of the physical start inside its page, reserves a page-aligned window for the expanded length, maps the window, and returns window start plus original offset so hypervisor and physical views share sub-page alignment.

Vector installation chooses a base from the requested hardening slot, using linked blobs for direct modes and a previously established hardened base for indirect modes, rejects unknown slots, converts the base through slot addressing, and stores the result in per-CPU vector storage. Early mapping reuses the linked blob when idmapped vectors are unneeded and otherwise creates an executable private copy and records its base.

Stack allocation reserves twice the architectural extent aligned to its own size, maps only the upper half as hypervisor memory while leaving the lower half unbacked as a guard, and returns the address past the reservation. Failure of table installation restores the prior allocation cursor. Alignment ensures a dedicated bit distinguishes valid stack addresses from guard addresses for overflow detection.
The protected register descriptor array must be strictly increasing under its comparator. Verification scans adjacent pairs from the second entry and reports disorder distinctly from success.

Handles encode table index plus a fixed offset, so values below the offset are invalid. Free search scans linearly for an empty slot up to a maximum and signals exhaustion. Reservation converts the found index to a handle, while release and initialization convert handles back and validate range before acting.

Finalization snapshots host translation controls from the host MMU, enables translation plus optionally hardware coherency when advertised, flushes parameters to point of coherency with ordering against in-flight walks, reloads stage two, applies an errata-dependent barrier, invalidates cached translation state, and orders completion. It fails without side effects when translation is already recorded as enabled.

Initialization requires at least one created CPU and a handle carrying the required offset, sizes the descriptor from CPU count and the root from host controls, maps donated descriptor and root regions with alignment and donation checks, initializes descriptor state and stage two, and publishes into the table only as the final step. Failures destroy stage two where created, unmap donations, and unpin host memory.

Descriptor setup always inherits the host counter value and interrupt model, clears flags before selective restore, copies host translation controls, links architecture and table state, and assigns an identifier one greater than the index with zero reserved for the host. Non-protected guests inherit broad flags and features while protected guests inherit only an allowed subset gated by per-extension permissions, with SVE presence reflected in a dedicated flag.

Pool setup bounds maximum order by pool size and a global limit, initializes one free list per order, records interval bounds, marks every page as refcounted order zero, and returns pages beyond a reserved prefix to the pool. Release returns a page only when its reference count reaches zero. Buddy computation flips the bit for the given size and rejects out-of-range results, while availability additionally requires matching order and zero references.

Guest stage-two setup builds a pool from donated root pages, installs guest-aware allocation plus conversion plus reference plus cache helpers, initializes the table under a component guard, and records the physical root. Teardown under the same guard destroys the full covered range and clears the recorded address. Root release frees the exact root extent and nulls the reference after unlinking.

A global page-table guard serializes private range reservation and stack creation. The low-level reservation requires the guard to be held, the public reservation acquires it around cursor sampling and update, and stack creation holds it across alignment plus reservation plus installation while saving the prior cursor for rollback on failure.

A global VM table guard serializes slot reservation plus installation plus removal. Reservation and installation acquire it around the update, release acquires it around conditional clearing, and internal allocate plus install plus remove helpers require it to be already held.

A per-VM component guard serializes stage-two initialization and destruction around pagetable calls. Each buddy pool carries its own guard initialized during pool setup. Per-CPU vector and boot-parameter updates rely on per-CPU isolation in the shown fragments.

A pool descriptor holds a guard plus maximum order plus an array of list heads indexed by order plus interval bounds. A page descriptor holds an order plus a reference count. Pages beyond the reserved prefix live on order lists, with only the head of a compound extent carrying a valid order and followers marked with a sentinel.

Free-list linkage reuses the memory of the free page itself as the list node obtained through page-to-address conversion. Removal unlinks and clears the embedded node while insertion initializes the embedded node and appends it to the selected order list.

A stage-two descriptor records address width plus start level plus memory operations plus owning MMU plus flags plus an optional forcing callback plus the allocated root. Guest operations bind exact and single allocation plus exact freeing plus address conversion plus reference counting plus cache and instruction-cache maintenance to guest-aware helpers.

A hypervisor VM descriptor links the host VM pointer plus CPU count plus protection state plus architecture controls plus stage-two MMU plus table plus pool plus guard. Setup wires the MMU back to architecture and table state and sizes the descriptor from a base plus one pointer per CPU with overflow-checked arithmetic.

Each slot starts empty, moves to a reserved marker on reservation, moves to an installed descriptor on successful initialization which publishes the VM, and returns to empty on removal or on release of a still-reserved slot. Installation requires the reserved state and release acts only on the reserved state; missing tables, out-of-range indices and mismatched states are rejected.

Host protection moves from unprotected to protected exactly once per CPU when recorded translation enablement changes from clear to set alongside snapshotted controls. A later attempt observes the set state and aborts without touching hardware.

Attachment zeroes the candidate extent, treats out-of-range pages as unmergeable order zero, otherwise repeatedly merges with an available same-order buddy while clearing merged orders and retaining the lower address as head, then records the final order on the head and queues it on the matching free list.

Defensive checks cover a missing table, exhausted slots, invalid handles, zero CPU counts, unaligned or undonatable regions, private range overflow, mapping failures and unordered descriptors. Table absence yields an error or silent return rather than dereference, initialization failures unwind mappings and pins in reverse order, and stack mapping failure restores the allocation cursor.

Handle encoding adds a fixed offset to the table index, table capacity bounds search and validation, a reserved marker is distinct from empty and installed values, descriptor sizing is a base plus one pointer per CPU with checked arithmetic, and stack reservation doubles the architectural size with base aligned to the doubled size.

Executable hypervisor protection applies to vectors and identity code while plain hypervisor protection applies to stacks and save areas. Host finalization programs translation enablement plus optional coherency. Identifier zero is reserved for the host with guests numbered from one. VA partitioning places I/O in the lower half of a non-conflicting quarter and the vmemmap in the upper half.

Host SVE mapping is skipped when the platform lacks the feature, otherwise each CPU maps its host save area sized by a helper and rounded to page granularity. Boot refresh writes the live table root address into each per-CPU record and cleans the record to point of coherency.
